headline: Chips Drag, Software Leads: Tuesday Opens in the Shadow of a Fractured Tech Trade
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious open on Tuesday after Monday's session revealed a market increasingly willing to rotate away from semiconductor names and toward software and consumer plays. Breadth in our 501-stock universe was constructive — 319 advancers against 179 decliners — yet the headline number masked a sharp divergence: the Software sector gained 3.19% while Semiconductors shed 1.49% and Energy fell 2.13%, leaving the session's complexion decidedly mixed.

The week's dominant macro catalyst sits squarely at the Federal Reserve. Prediction markets on Kalshi are already parsing the precise language Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is expected to deploy, with traders debating whether his remarks lean toward 'oil' or 'shock' as a framing device for current conditions. Bitcoin ETFs broke a multi-session inflow streak Monday as rate-path anxiety reasserted itself, a signal that risk appetite remains conditional. Crude oil futures, meanwhile, are pricing market adaptability rather than optimism around a potential Iran peace, according to Reuters dispatches.

At the open, watch staffing, software, and telehealth names that surged Monday for follow-through conviction. The semiconductor complex — battered by broad losses across memory, equipment, and chip-design names — faces further headline risk tied to a reported nine-figure artificial-intelligence infrastructure deal still taking shape overnight. Apple quietly reclaimed the title of world's most valuable publicly traded company by session's end, a shift worth monitoring as the AI trade reprices around it.

briefs.headline: Fed Chair's Word Choice Becomes the Week's Macro Pivot
briefs.body: Prediction-market platform Kalshi shows traders actively wagering on whether Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will characterize current conditions in hawkish or cautious terms this week. The debate is nuanced enough that specific word choices — not just rate signals — are moving positioning. Bitcoin ETF outflows Monday suggest the rate-sensitive corner of the market is already hedging.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Bears the Brunt as AI Infrastructure Deal Clouds Picture
briefs.body: Memory, equipment, and chip-design names were the session's hardest-hit cohort Monday, with the Semiconductors sector dropping 1.49% as a group. Separately, reports of a potential nine-figure data-center financing arrangement involving a major AI chipmaker added complexity to the narrative, with analysts framing the deal as a headwind rather than a tailwind for the broader AI trade.

briefs.headline: Apple Reclaims the Crown as World's Most Valuable Company
briefs.body: Apple ended Monday's session as the highest market-capitalization company on the planet, displacing a prominent chipmaker that had held the title. The shift underscores a broader rotation dynamic in which mega-cap technology leadership is being reshuffled rather than abandoned, and gives investors a new reference point heading into a busy week of corporate and macro catalysts.

briefs.headline: OpenAI's Washington Offensive Takes Shape Ahead of Key Meetings
briefs.body: OpenAI chief Sam Altman is scheduled to meet with members of the Trump administration and several U.S. senators this week, with prepared remarks already signaling his intended message. The meetings arrive as the company's infrastructure ambitions — including a reported half-trillion-dollar data-center leasing arrangement — attract mounting scrutiny from both regulators and capital markets.

briefs.headline: Staffing Rebound and Beauty Surge Lead Monday's Unlikely Winners
briefs.body: Robert Half surged 12.61% to pace all gainers in our universe, while e.l.f. Beauty climbed 8.60% and Manhattan Associates added 8.04% after apparent earnings or guidance catalysts. The moves illustrate Monday's central theme: when large-cap technology stumbled, capital found traction in staffing, consumer cosmetics, and supply-chain software rather than staying on the sidelines.

briefs.headline: Logistics and Trucking Names Extend Industrial Sector's Weak Underbelly
briefs.body: Despite Industrials posting a modest 0.33% aggregate gain Monday, the sector masked significant internal stress. Heartland Express fell 7.69% and C.H. Robinson dropped 6.46%, suggesting freight and logistics operators are absorbing pressure from soft volume trends or deteriorating rate environments. The divergence with staffing names like Robert Half highlights how heterogeneous the industrial landscape has become.
